statement.p: Calculate the derivative using the appropriate rule or combination of rules. f(x)=\frac{e^{x}}{\left(e^{x}+5\right)\mathopen{}\left(x+4\right)}

static.solution: f'(x) we begin with quotient rule f'(x)= \frac{(e^x+5)(x+4)\frac{d}{dx}[e^x]-e^x\frac{d}{dx}[(e^x+5)(x+4)]}{((e^x+5)(x+4))^2}. Next, recall that \frac{d}{dx}[e^x]=e^x, and use the product rule to compute \frac{d}{dx}[(e^x+5)(x+4)]=\frac{d}{dx}[e^x+5](x+4)+(e^x+5)\frac{d}{dx}[x+4] which is (e^x)(x+4)+(e^x+5)(1). Therefore f'(x)= \frac{(e^x+5)(x+4)\cdot e^x-e^x\cdot (e^x(x+4)+(e^x+5))}{((e^x+5)(x+4))^2} and after factoring out e^x in the numerator, expanding (e^x+5)(x+4)=xe^x+4\cdot e^x+5 x+5\cdot 4, and distributing the minus sign, we get f'(x)=\frac{e^x(xe^x+5 x+4 e^x - xe^x-4 e^x-e^x-5)}{((e^x+5)(x+4))^2} which simplifies to f'(x)=\frac{e^x(5 x - e^x-5)}{((e^x+5)(x+4))^2}.
